summary: Cast-iron skeleton rear range light at Billingsport, Paulsboro, lit 31 Dec 1880 to guide Delaware River traffic; still an active aid.

light.characteristic: fixed red (since 1983; fixed white with red sector 1908-1983)

lens.where: original optic; present optic a DCB-24 (NRHP 2005)

access.note: Grounds open; the tower is open during periodic tours run by the Tinicum Rear Range Lighthouse Society.

facts.agency: U.S. Coast Guard (owner); leased to the Borough of Paulsboro

events.note: High day mark renewed and raised above the tower
Tower repainted black; slatted frames added below the watch room
Fixed red changed to fixed white with a red sector
Per LighthouseFriends; the nomination gives about 1967 (see next event)
Last keeper John Birch stayed on as custodian until 1945 (LighthouseFriends)
Keeper Clyde Harrison died February 1965; the nomination ties this to the rear light, LighthouseFriends to the front light
Per the nomination (about 1967); station buildings demolished
Repainted; handrails repaired (Coast Guard, per LighthouseFriends)
Tours resumed in September 2018 after the tower was repaired and repainted

keepers.name: Clyde Harrison
keepers.note: Named by the NRHP nomination as the keeper whose death in February 1965 prompted replacement discussions for this rear light. LighthouseFriends (from a family member's recollection) and the USLHS front-light roster (Clyde S. Harrison 1944-1965) place him at the front light. Listed here because the nomination names him; the conflict is not settled. See notes_for_editor.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record says sources differ on whether the light is still lit. The 2005 nomination calls it 'an active aid to navigation' and LighthouseFriends says the light is a fixed red light today, so it is lit.
The light was lit 31 Dec 1880 with Hannold as keeper (nomination, LighthouseFriends). LighthouseFriends lists his stint from 1881, and the USLHS roster from 1880.

notes_for_editor: 1) Record conflicts not settled here: the record's characteristic 'Iso R 2s' (Wikidata) does not match the fixed red in the 2005 nomination and LighthouseFriends; its range 30 nm and focal height 34.0 m are not sourced (LighthouseFriends quotes an 1890 range of 8.5 nm and a height of 109 ft). 2) The record's structure list (front_range steel 1880 5.2 m; rear 24.4 m and 26.0 m) does not match the nomination's rear tower of 86 ft (26.2 m); the front light's history (1880 dwelling, 1887 frame tower, 1908 offshore tower) is a different structure and should be checked against its own record. 3) Automation: LighthouseFriends says 1933 (custodian to 1945); the nomination says around 1967. Both are kept as events, not reconciled. 4) Clyde Harrison: the nomination ties his February 1965 death to this rear light; LighthouseFriends and the USLHS front roster place him at the front light. Not put on the rear roster. 5) Roster: the USLHS rear list has four lines (1880-1933); the matched place is tinicum-island-range-rear by slug (not coordinates). The front place roster (11 lines) is a different place and was not merged. 6) The 1880 Light-House Board report (pp. 271-273), cited by the nomination for the appropriation and the 1880 tower money, was not read directly; those facts are footnoted to the nomination. 7) Corpus: the Lighthouse Board volumes in the local corpus cover 1891-1901 only; the 1897 and 1901 entries were read from them. The 1908 characteristic change and the 1983 change are from the nomination, which cites Light Lists. 8) Chronicling America search 'Tinicum range' in NJ papers, 1880-1930: no hits. No storm, wreck or rescue tied to this light was found, so the story has no 'Storms, wrecks and rescues' chapter. 9) Not used: Wikipedia (lead only), loc.gov (not read). Confidence is medium because of the automation and Harrison conflicts. 10) Fact-check 2026-10-22: the story reports two dates for the Delaware's first ranges. The NRHP nomination dates the river's range complex to 1876 (Deepwater Point and New Castle ranges) and lists Tinicum Island among the 1880 ranges; the 1938 Lighthouse Service Bulletin article (PDF p. 13, printed p. 109) says the first ranges on the Delaware were established in 1880 and names Tinicum Island and Mifflin Bar. Both are kept; not reconciled. 11) The 1897 day-mark raise: the NRHP gives 35 feet and LighthouseFriends quotes the report as 25 feet; the figure is garbled in the OCR, so the story gives no height. 12) Clyde Harrison roster line: kept with a note because the nomination names him; the story says so rather than placing him on the rear roster silently. 13) Entry numbers (465 for 1897, 618 for 1901) are the report's item numbers read from the OCR, cited with scan pages checked by corpus.py page.
